ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Human albinism is an autosomal recessive genetic disease. The pedigree of a certain patient's family is shown in Figure A. It is known that a certain method can make the normal gene A show one band, while the albinism gene a shows a different other band. Using this method to analyze each individual in the above family, the presence or absence of bands and their positions are marked in Figure B. According to the above experimental results, please answer the following question: Based only on the information of individual genotypes in Figure B, if mutation factors are not considered, what is the probability that individual 9 marries an albino patient outside the family and gives birth to an albino child?

Using this method to analyze each individual in the above family, the presence or absence of bands and their positions are marked in Figure B. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure A is the pedigree of this family, and Figure B is the band detection result of individuals numbered 1—13. In Figure B, the horizontal numbers correspond to individuals 1 to 13, and the left side marks “band 1” and “band 2.” According to the explanation in the stem, band 1 corresponds to the normal gene A, and band 2 corresponds to the albinism gene a. Observing the column for individual 9 in Figure B, there is only band 1 and no band 2, so individual 9 is detected as having only the normal gene A. Then reason: Based only on the genotype information in Figure B, the genotype of individual 9 is AA. Albinism is an autosomal recessive genetic disease, and the genotype of an albino patient outside the family must be aa. In a mating between AA and aa, all offspring have genotype Aa and are carriers, and no aa albino children will appear. Therefore, the probability of giving birth to an albino child is 0.
